title: Why a steel ship floats but a steel bar sinks
examples: How can a heavy steel ship float?
Why does a ship sink lower when loaded?

forces.label: Weight
forces.ask: Why does a ship sink lower when it is loaded?

explain.say: Steel is about eight times denser than water, so a steel bar sinks straight away. Yet a ship made of tens of thousands of tonnes of steel floats. Two forces decide it: weight and upthrust.

draw.text: Why a steel ship floats but a steel bar sinks

forces.label: Weight
forces.ask: Why does a ship sink lower when it is loaded?

explain.say: The ship's weight pulls it down into the water. As it settles, its hull pushes water out of the way, and the water pushes back up.

forces.label: Weight
forces.ask: Why does a ship sink lower when it is loaded?

explain.say: That upward push, called upthrust or buoyancy, equals the weight of the water pushed aside. The ship sinks lower until it has pushed aside water weighing exactly as much as it does, and then it floats.

forces.label: Weight
forces.ask: Why does a ship sink lower when it is loaded?

explain.say: A solid bar pushes aside only its own small volume of water, far lighter than the steel. A hull is mostly air inside, so it pushes aside a huge volume of water, enough to balance its weight. If water floods in, that air is lost and the ship sinks.

faq.q: Why does a ship sink lower when it is loaded?
faq.a: Extra cargo adds weight, so the ship settles deeper until it pushes aside enough extra water to balance it. Load lines painted on the hull show how deep it may safely sit.
Upthrust, or buoyancy, is the upward push of water on anything in it. It equals the weight of the water the object pushes aside, an idea called Archimedes' principle.

faq.q: Why does a steel bar sink?
faq.a: A solid bar pushes aside only its own volume of water, and that water weighs about an eighth as much as the steel. The weight wins, so it sinks.

faq.q: How does the hull shape help a ship float?
faq.a: The hull wraps a large space full of air, so on average the ship is much less dense than water. It can push aside a big volume of water while weighing relatively little.

faq.q: Why does a ship sink if it floods?
faq.a: Water pouring in replaces the air inside the hull, so the ship gets heavier without pushing aside any more water. Ships are divided into watertight compartments so one leak cannot flood the whole hull.

facts: Archimedes' principle: the upthrust on an object equals the weight of fluid it pushes aside.
Steel is about eight times denser than water.
Ships float slightly higher in salty seawater than in fresh river water, because seawater is denser.
